segments.de:
Disclosure of product information for financial products that are marketed on the basis of environmental or social characteristics on the website

relating to the open-ended domestic special AIF with fixed investment terms, in the form of a special sub-fund with a primary investment focus on property and bearing the name

“W&W Real Estate International 1”

a. Summary

This financial product (the “Fund”) promotes environmental characteristics but does not have a sustainable investment objective. The investments underlying this financial product do not take into account the EU criteria for environmentally sustainable economic activities as defined in the Taxonomy Regulation. This financial product does not take into account the most significant adverse impacts on sustainability factors. The financial product aims to hold a diversified property portfolio. At least 51 per cent of the lettable area of the properties managed by the Fund must hold a third-party sustainability certification recognised by GRESB, i.e. they have obtained certification under one of the building certification schemes listed in Annex 5a of GRESB’s annual Real Estate Standard and Reference Guide. The financial product plans to invest exclusively in property and, where applicable, property companies whose scope of business is generally limited to the holding and management of property and which have no employees.

b. No sustainable investment objective

This financial product promotes environmental characteristics but does not aim to make sustainable investments.

c. Environmental characteristics of the financial product

The fund promotes investment in properties of which at least 51 per cent, based on the fund’s managed lettable area, hold a third-party sustainability certification recognised by GRESB. These certifications take environmental characteristics into account in particular. GRESB (‘Global Real Estate Sustainability Benchmark’) is an internationally recognised organisation that assesses and compares property portfolios and investments against ESG criteria in terms of their sustainability and ESG performance. The assessment framework and methodology are refined each year to ensure that the ESG benchmarks remain aligned with the latest best practices and market trends in the sector (https://www.gresb.com/nl-en/). The comprehensive list of sustainability certifications recognised by GRESB can be found in GRESB’s annual Real Estate Standard and Reference Guide (Appendix 5a).

d. Investment strategy

The financial product aims to achieve a diversified portfolio of properties, taking into account its General and Specific Investment Conditions as well as its investment strategy. At least 51 per cent of the lettable area of the properties managed by the fund must hold a third-party sustainability certification recognised by GRESB, i.e. they must have obtained certification under one of the building certification schemes listed in Appendix 5a of GRESB’s annual Real Estate Standard and Reference Guide. The financial product plans to invest exclusively in property and, where applicable, property companies whose scope of business is generally limited to the holding and management of property and which have no employees. The financial product will not invest in commercial enterprises; consequently, a corresponding assessment of good governance practices is not required.

e. Allocation of investments

In accordance with its investment strategy, the financial product will invest exclusively in the property asset class. At least 51 per cent, based on the lettable area of the properties, must hold a third-party certification recognised by GRESB. A maximum of 49 per cent, based on the lettable area of the properties, may not hold such certification.

f. Monitoring of environmental characteristics

The respective ratings/awards for the property certifications mentioned under d) (investment strategy) serve as sustainability indicators. The underlying data is monitored on an ongoing basis. Compliance with the required thresholds for maintaining the respective certifications is also monitored on an ongoing basis.

g. Methods

The Fund’s sustainability criteria are met if at least 51 per cent of the investments in property, based on lettable area, are made in properties that hold a third-party certification recognised by GRESB.

h. Data sources and processing

The property-specific data required to obtain the certifications referred to under d) (Investment Strategy) is usually provided by sellers during the acquisition process via a digital data room. The data contained therein is generally reviewed and validated as part of technical, legal, tax and economic due diligence. The individual due diligence processes are carried out by specialists such as engineers, solicitors, tax advisers and auditors. During the management phase, the property-specific data is provided and processed by the relevant utility company, Asset Manager or Property Manager, as well as by technical advisers where applicable. Estimates will therefore largely be dispensed with.

i. Restrictions regarding methods and data

The financial product does not impose any restrictions regarding methods and data.

j. Duty of care

All of the fund’s investments are reviewed during the pre-acquisition due diligence phase (and on an ongoing basis during management) to ensure compliance with the requirements for obtaining and/or maintaining the certifications referred to in d). The results of these reviews will be used to assess the investments and, where necessary, any required divestments.

k. Engagement policy

The financial product plans to invest exclusively in property and, where applicable, property companies that do not conduct their own operational business. The financial product will not invest in commercial enterprises, which is why the issue of engagement policy is not relevant to this financial product.

l. Specific benchmark

No overarching benchmark has been defined.

This product information was initially published on 11 December 2023.

Change history:

19 June 2024: Addition of the fund’s ISIN number and the initial publication date.

segments.en:
Disclosure of product information for financial products that promote environmental or social characteristics on the website

regarding the open-ended domestic special AIF with fixed investment conditions in the form of a special investment fund with an investment focus on real estate and the name

“W&W Real Estate International 1“

a. Summary

This financial product (the „Fund“) promotes environmental characteristics but does not have a sustainable investment objective. The investments underlying this financial product do not take into account the EU criteria for environmentally sustainable economic activities within the meaning of the Taxonomy Regulation. This financial product does not take into account the main adverse impacts on sustainability factors. The financial product aims for a diversified real estate portfolio. At least 51 % of the lettable area under management by the financial product have a third-party sustainability certification recognized by GRESB, i.e. obtained a certification under one of the building certification schemes set out in Appendix 5a of GRESB’s annual Real Estate Standard and Reference Guide). The financial product only plans investments in properties and possibly property companies whose scope of business is fundamentally limited to holding and managing properties and which have no employees.

b. No sustainable investment objective

This financial product promotes ecological characteristics but does not aim for sustainable investments.

c. Environmental or social characteristics of the financial product

The fund advertises that it invests in properties, at least 51 % of which, based on the lettable area under management by the financial product have a third-party sustainability certification recognized by GRESB. These certifications take particularly ecological characteristics into account. GRESB („Global Real Estate Sustainability Benchmark“) is an internationally recognized organization that evaluates the sustainability performance of real estate portfolio and assets. The assessment framework and methodology evolves each year to ensure the benchmark is aligned with emerging best practices and market trends in the industry (https://www.gresb.com/nl-en/). The comprehensive list of the sustainability certifications recognized by GRESB can be found in GRESB’s annual Real Estate Standard and Reference Guide (Appendix 5a).

d. Investment strategy

The financial product aims to achieve a diversified real estate portfolio, taking into account its General and Special Terms of Investment and its investment strategy. At least 51 % of the lettable area under management by the financial product have a third-party sustainability certification recognized by GRESB, i.e. obtained a certification under one of the building certification schemes set out in Appendix 5a of GRESB’s annual Real Estate Standard and Reference Guide). The financial product only plans investments in properties and possibly property companies whose scope of business is fundamentally limited to holding and managing properties and which have no employees. The financial product will not invest in commercial companies, which is why a corresponding assessment of good governance practices is not required.

e. Allocation of investments

In accordance with its investment strategy, the financial product will invest exclusively in the property asset class. At least 51% in terms of the rental space of the properties have a third-party sustainability certification recognized by GRESB. A maximum of 49% of the rental space of the properties have no certification.

f. Monitoring of environmental or social characteristics

The respective ratings/awards of the property certifications mentioned under d) (investment strategy) serve as sustainability indicators. The data on which these are based is monitored on an ongoing basis. Compliance with the values required to maintain the respective certifications is also monitored on an ongoing basis.

g. Methods

The fund’s sustainability criteria are met if at least 51% of the investments in properties in relation to the rental space are made in properties that have a third-party sustainability certification recognized by GRESB.

h. Data sources and processing

The property-specific data required to obtain the certifications mentioned under d) (investment strategy) is usually provided by the seller during the purchase process via a digital data room. The data contained therein is reviewed and checked for plausibility as part of technical, legal, tax and economic due diligence. The individual due diligence processes are carried out by specialists such as engineers, lawyers, tax advisors and auditors. In the management phase, the property-specific data is provided and processed by the respective utility company, asset or property manager and, if necessary, technical consultants. Estimates are therefore largely dispensed with.

i. Limitations with regard to methods and data

The financial product does not impose any limitations in terms of methods and data.

j. Due Diligence

All of the fund’s investments are reviewed during the purchase due diligence phase (and on an ongoing basis during management) with regard to obtaining and/or maintaining the certifications mentioned under d). The results of the reviews are used to evaluate the investments and any necessary divestments.

k. Participation Policy

The financial product only plans investments in properties and possibly property companies that do not have their own business operations. The financial product will not invest in commercial companies, which is why the topic of participation policy is not relevant for this financial product.

l. Specified Benchmark

An overall benchmark has not been defined.

This product information was initially published on 11.12.2023.

History of changes:

19/06/2024: Addition of the ISIN number of the fund and the initial publication date.
